vulnerability.name: USN-9214-1
vulnerability.description: It was discovered that the GNU binutils gold linker incorrectly handled certain ELF files. A local attacker could possibly use this issue to cause GNU binutils to crash, resulting in a denial of service. This issue only affected Ubuntu 22.04 LTS. (CVE-2019-1010204)  Han Zheng discovered that GNU binutils incorrectly handled demangling certain Rust symbols. A local attacker could possibly use this issue to cause GNU binutils to crash, resulting in a denial of service. This issue only affected Ubuntu 22.04 LTS. (CVE-2022-27943)  It was discovered that GNU binutils incorrectly handled certain DWARF debug information. A local attacker could possibly use this issue to cause GNU binutils to use excessive resources, leading to a denial of service. This issue only affected Ubuntu 22.04 LTS. (CVE-2022-48064)  It was discovered that the GNU binutils linker did not properly free memory under certain circumstances. A local attacker could possibly use this issue to cause GNU binutils to use excessive resources, leading to a denial of service. This issue only affected Ubuntu 22.04 LTS and Ubuntu 24.04 LTS. (CVE-2025-1150)  It was discovered that the GNU binutils linker incorrectly handled certain TLS relocations on x86 systems, leading to a heap-based buffer overflow. A local attacker could possibly use this issue to cause GNU binutils to crash, resulting in a denial of service. This issue only affected Ubuntu 22.04 LTS and Ubuntu 24.04 LTS. (CVE-2025-11495)  It was discovered that GNU binutils incorrectly handled certain malformed DWARF debug information, leading to an infinite loop. A local attacker could possibly use these issues to cause GNU binutils to use excessive resources, leading to a denial of service. These issues only affected Ubuntu 24.04 LTS. (CVE-2025-69644, CVE-2025-69646)  It was discovered that GNU binutils incorrectly handled certain malformed DWARF debug information. A local attacker could possibly use these issues to cause GNU binutils to crash, resulting in a denial of service. These issues only affected Ubuntu 22.04 LTS and Ubuntu 24.04 LTS. (CVE-2025-69645, CVE-2025-69652)  It was discovered that GNU binutils incorrectly handled certain XCOFF object files, leading to out-of-bounds reads. A local attacker could possibly use these issues to cause GNU binutils to crash, resulting in a denial of service, or obtain sensitive information. (CVE-2026-3441, CVE-2026-3442, CVE-2026-4647, CVE-2026-15003)  It was discovered that the GNU binutils linker incorrectly handled certain XCOFF object files, leading to a heap-based buffer overflow. A local attacker could possibly use this issue to cause GNU binutils to crash, resulting in a denial of service, or possibly execute arbitrary code. (CVE-2026-6846)  It was discovered that the GNU binutils linker incorrectly handled memory when a linker plugin claimed an archive member, leading to a use-after-free. A local attacker could possibly use this issue to cause GNU binutils to crash, resulting in a denial of service, or possibly execute arbitrary code. (CVE-2026-19548)  It was discovered that the GNU binutils linker incorrectly handled certain invalid relocations on x86 systems, leading to a buffer overflow. A local attacker could possibly use this issue to cause GNU binutils to crash, resulting in a denial of service. (CVE-2026-90803)  It was discovered that the GNU binutils linker incorrectly handled certain orphan sections. A local attacker could possibly use this issue to cause GNU binutils to crash, resulting in a denial of service. This issue only affected Ubuntu 24.04 LTS and Ubuntu 26.04 LTS. (CVE-2026-90828)  It was discovered that the GNU binutils linker incorrectly handled certain object files on x86 systems, leading to NULL pointer dereferences. A local attacker could possibly use these issues to cause GNU binutils to crash, resulting in a denial of service. (CVE-2026-91781, CVE-2026-91782)

statements.status_notes: Several security issues were fixed in GNU binutils.
